turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Morning.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's start with your full name and date of birth. Brendan Gallagher,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: August 30th, 1974.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Brendan. Big weekend coming up.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My daughter, Siobhan, has a soccer tournament in Canton, so I'll be freezing on the sidelines all Saturday.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Bring a thermos, so this is your yearly physical. Anything bothering you or new since last year? Honestly, I feel fine. No complaints.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Well, I want to talk about the smoking. I think I'm ready to quit for real.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm really glad to hear that.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: We'll spend some time on it. How much are you smoking right now?" About a pack a day. I started when I was twenty -two, so about thirty years.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Have you tried quitting before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, in two thousand nineteen I used the patch and made it six months. Then work got stressful and I picked it back up. Six months is a real accomplishment. It means you can do it. Any cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Nope, none of those. Any blood in your stool or weight loss you can't explain? No. Alcohols?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two or three beers a week, maybe.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any family history changes?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My mum had breast cancer back in 2021. She did chemo, she's doing great now.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Dad's fine,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: he's 80 and still golfing. Glad she's doing well.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You're not on any regular medicines, right?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nothing. Just a multivitamin most days. And no allergies to medications? Not that I know of.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Your blood pressure is one hundred thirty -two over eighty -two, pulse seventy -eight, and weight is two hundred five pounds.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let me listen.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Heart is regular, no murmurs. Lungs are clear, no wheezing. Belly is soft and non -tender.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No swelling in your legs.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Everything looks good.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'll take it. Now, a few screening things.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You've never had a colonoscopy, right? Never.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I keep putting it off.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You're 52, so you do.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'll put in a referral to gastroenterology for a screening colonoscopy, and because you've smoked about 30 pack years, you qualify for a yearly low -dose CT scan at the chest to screen for lung cancer. I'll order that, too.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, makes sense. And I'd like fasting labs,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: a cholesterol panel, and an A1C to check for diabetes. Your tetanus shot was two thousand twenty, so you're up to date there.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: We do have the flu shot today, would you like it? Sure, go ahead.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Great, the nurse will give you the flu shot in your left arm before you leave.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, the smoking. Let's pick a quit date. How about November 1st? That's a Sunday.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: November 1st?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, yeah. Since a pack a day is heavy,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: start the twenty -one milligram nicotine patch that morning, one patch a day and use nicotine gum two milligrams when you get a craving.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You can buy both over the counter. Get rid of the lighters and ashtrays and figure out what you'll do instead after meals and in the car,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: that's when people slip. You can also call the quit line, 1 -800 -Quit Now for free coaching. The car is the big one for me.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep gum in the cup holder then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: We spent about eight minutes on this and it's the most important thing you'll do for your health. I'll see you in one month to check how the quit is going and we'll go over the labs then.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Sounds good.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thanks, Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Zhu. You're welcome. Good luck to Siobhan this weekend.
